pages.text: $(li)$(item)Transmitter Dish$()$(br)$(li)$(item)Receiver Dish$()$(br)$(li)$(item)Range Module I$()$(br)$(li)$(item)Range Module II$()$(br)$(li)$(item)Range Module III$()$(br)$(li)$(item)Infinity Range Module$()

Dishes send $(l)FE through the air$(), to places a cable can't reach: across a valley, to an outpost, even into another dimension. A $(l)Transmitter Dish$() sends, a $(l)Receiver Dish$() receives, and a $(l)Range Module$() in the transmitter sets how far and how much.

There is no beam to see. A Transmitter Dish is working when it turns to a receiver and $(l)holds still$() while it sends. A Receiver Dish is getting power when the rings of its dish $(l)light up$() from the rim to the centre.

$(l)Building$()$(br)$(li)It is a small multiblock. Place it with $(l)three$() $(l:basics/cyber_frame)Cyber Frames$(/l): on its right as you face it, behind it, and in the corner between. The dish unfolds on its turret over a 2x2 base.
pages.title: Transmitter Dish

pages.text: $(li)Placed alone, a right-click sends out drones that show where the frames go.$(br)$(li)Feed it FE with $(l:cables/energy_conduit)Energy Conduits$(/l) on the dish block.$(br)$(l)Using it$()$(br2)Each Transmitter Dish runs $(l)one network$(). Its GUI has two tabs on the left of the network panel:

$(li)$(l)Network$(): the network's $(l)name$(), its $(l)colour$() (which lights the indicator on both dishes) and its access.$(br)$(li)$(l)Manage$(): switches charging players' Energy Spheres on or off (owner only, see below).$(br)Access decides who may link a receiver:$(br)$(li)$(l)Private (new networks)$(): only you

$(li)$(l)Team$(): you and the players on your team$(br)$(li)$(l)Public$(): anyone$(br)A team is a vanilla /team, an FTB Teams team or an Open Parties and Claims party. Only you and your team can change the network's name, colour and access.$(br2)$(l)How it sends$()

$(li)It serves up to $(l)4 receivers in turn$(): it turns to one (1 second), sends for 4 seconds, then moves to the next.$(br)$(li)The signal passes through blocks, but the chunks of both dishes must be loaded.$(br)$(li)A tenth of the FE is $(l)lost on the way$().

$(li)With a receiver in another dimension, both dishes point $(l)straight up at the sky$().$(br)$(li)A receiver the transmitter no longer reaches (after a swap to a weaker Range Module, say) loses its seat on the network after $(l)30 seconds$(), so swapping a module is safe.
$(li)It is a small multiblock two blocks tall: put $(l)a Cyber Frame on top$() of it and its dish unfolds.
pages.title: Receiver Dish

pages.text: $(li)Its GUI lists the networks it can reach, with their colour, distance (or dimension) and seats taken, for example "2/4". $(l)Click$() one to link. A full network is greyed out. $(l)Disconnect$() leaves it.$(br)$(li)The GUI also shows the FE/t arriving.
$(li)It gives what it receives to the blocks and conduits around it.

The Transmitter Dish has $(l)one module slot$(). The module sets how far it reaches and how much FE per tick it sends in all, shared among its receivers.$(br)$(li)$(l)None$(): 32 blocks, 2,000$(br)$(li)$(l)Range Module I$(): 128 blocks, 8,000$(br)$(li)$(l)Range Module II$(): 512 blocks, 32,000
pages.title: Range Modules

pages.text: $(li)$(l)Range Module III$(): 2,048 blocks, 128,000$(br)$(li)$(l)Infinity Range Module$(): Unlimited, into other dimensions, Unlimited

A Transmitter Dish also charges the $(l:trinkets/energy_sphere)Energy Sphere$(/l) on your $(l:trinkets/utility_belt)Utility Belt$(/l) from afar, for players in its reach:$(br)$(li)on a Private network, only its owner;$(br)$(li)on a Team network, the team too;$(br)$(li)on a Public network, everyone.
pages.title: Charging your Energy Sphere

pages.text: It sends up to the module's power, losing 10% on the way. The players it charges take their turn with the receivers, so now and then the dish turns to follow you. The owner can switch this off in the $(l)Manage$() tab.

$(li)$(l)Transmitter Dish$(): 10 times its module's FE/t (at least 20,000 FE; 1,000,000,000 FE with the Infinity Range Module)$(br)$(li)$(l)Receiver Dish$(): 2,000,000 FE$(br)The Transmitter Dish takes in as much FE per tick as its module lets it send.
